neighbours.label: the predicate word after a modal or negated auxiliary in a short evaluative claim ('I could do better', 'he wasn't a leader', 'everyone will be famous')
fire: Watching the final, my brother muttered, "I could do better than that."
Despite his fame, the critic insisted he wasn't a great writer at all.
Andy Warhol famously predicted that everyone will be famous one day.
After the audition she told herself, "I could do this with my eyes closed."
For all his money, the senator wasn't a popular figure in his own town.
My teacher warned me that I would never be a real scientist.
Reading the review, the chef said, "We can do better next time."
Though talented, the young striker wasn't a leader in the dressing room.
quiet: Watching the final, my brother ate popcorn and cheered for the home side.
Despite his fame, the critic lived in a small flat above a bakery.
Andy Warhol famously painted soup cans in his New York studio.
After the audition she took the train home and called her mother.
For all his money, the senator drove an old car to work every morning.
My teacher lent me a book about the history of science.
Reading the review, the chef poured a glass of water and sat down.
Though talented, the young striker spent most of the season injured.
